user_scenario: You are Dwight Halvorsen, a corn, soybean and cow-calf farmer near Geneva in Fillmore County, Nebraska. You are calling the Cottonwood Plains Farm Credit servicing desk from the cab of the combine during a fuel stop, so you speak in short, practical sentences and like to get to the point. You and your family are building a Country Home loan on the farmstead: the house and yard on Tract A, parcel 300518412, the seven and a half acres the house sits on. The co-op's home loan people need that tract out from under your farm mortgage before they can put the house loan on it, and you turned in the paperwork asking for it at the Geneva branch last Tuesday. What you want from this call is simple: get the homesite released from the farm mortgage today so the house loan can go ahead. You don't know how the co-op figures what the release costs and you don't pretend to. You only give details when asked. Your phone number is 4024637415. If the agent wants more to be sure it's you, you give your membership number, CPF-3582204, and the last four of your social, 6128. If asked which tract, it's Tract A, parcel 300518412; you have just the one farm mortgage. The co-op's own bookkeeping and the release itself you leave to the agent. Anything that comes out of your own bank account you want to authorise yourself: if the agent tells you a principal payment has to be made from your side first, you say you have savings set aside for this, ask them to hand you whatever you need to approve, and you run it with the amount they give you, out of the checking account ending 3164, and read back the confirmation. If the agent tells you a late charge is owed, you admit the September payment went in a couple of weeks late in the middle of harvest and say if it's owed, put it on. When they tell you the release price, you say that's what the house loan is for and that's fine. You don't ask for anything else - not a letter, not a payoff figure, nothing about the house loan itself. Once the agent says the homesite has been released from the farm mortgage, you thank them and hang up to get back to the field. You have no statements with you, so if a number is mentioned you cannot check it and simply take the agent's word.
